## Overview

The **Starving Student Card Map** is an interactive deal-finding app that digitizes the physical Starving Student Discount Card — a booklet of 418 coupon-style deals across 199 Utah County businesses. Instead of flipping through a paper booklet, students open the app, see every deal pinned on a live map, and tap any location to get the full offer details and directions in under 10 seconds.

The primary purpose of this app is to:

- Help students find nearby deals at the exact moment they're deciding where to eat
- Replace a physical coupon booklet with a searchable, filterable, map-based experience
- Track how many uses remain on each deal across a student's card year

## Key Features

- **Interactive Map**: 819 pins across Utah County, clustered geographically and color-coded by category, with spiderfy behavior for densely co-located businesses
- **Deal Detail**: Tap any pin to see the full offer, usage tracker, address, expiration date, and one-tap Google Maps directions
- **Category Filtering**: Filter by Pizza, Restaurants, Sandwiches, Treats & Drinks, Free Stuff, Entertainment, and Retail & Auto
- **Search**: Find any business or deal by name instantly
- **Usage Tracking**: Dot-based tracker shows how many uses remain per deal, persisted locally so your history survives between sessions
- **Mobile-First Design**: Built for the on-the-go use case — full-screen map, bottom sheet deal details, and horizontally scrollable filters optimized for one-handed use

## Technical Details

**Framework/Stack**: Vite + React 19, Tailwind CSS, react-leaflet

**Data**: Static JSON (418 deals, built from a multi-stage Python geocoding pipeline)

**Deployment**: Vercel (auto-deploy from GitHub)

**Key Technologies**:

- Leaflet + react-leaflet-cluster for map rendering, clustering, and spiderfy
- Custom Python geocoding pipeline (5 scripts) to build and validate all 819 coordinates from a 376-row business CSV
- localStorage for client-side usage persistence with no backend required
- OpenStreetMap tiles for zero-cost map rendering

## What I Learned

Building the SSC Map taught me how much complexity hides inside "just put some pins on a map." The geocoding pipeline alone required several Python scripts and multiple fallback strategies to correctly place over 800 locations for 199 businesses across the Wasatch Front. On the frontend, getting clustering, spiderfy, and multi-deal location picking to work together required deep Leaflet customization that pushed me well beyond standard tutorials. The biggest product lesson came from user testing: watching someone struggle to find the directions button after using a deal showed me that the gap between "it works" and "it's usable" is where most of the real product work lives.
